A Love Other Than Yours: Seo Kang-joon & Ahn Eun-jin | K-Drama Interview | t2ONLINE

 Screen Actors Seo Kang-joon and Ahn Eun-jin chat with t2 about the unconventional love story that forms the heart of A Love Other Than Yours
 By Priyanka Roy 
 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 1:06AM | 4 min read Ahn Eun-jin as Lee Mi-do and Seo Kang-joon as Namgung Ho in A Love Other Than Yours, streaming on Prime Video
 Advertisement Romance is unconventional and relationships messy in A Love Other Than Yours . Airing on Prime Video, the 14 episodes of the Korean drama feelingly explore the slow but sure decay of a 10-year relationship where heady romance and initial excitement give way to a feeling of familiarity, taken-for-granted presence and, eventually, a sense of obligation.
 Pushed by family to either marry or break up, childhood sweethearts Namgung Ho and Lee Mi-do attempt an experimental one-month agreement to date other people. That, as expected, is the catalyst not only for the entry of other players into the story but also fuels further complications in the couple’s own relationship.
 Praised for delving into the messiness of relationships in a genre where conventional love stories are often par for course,  A Love Other Than Yours benefits from strong central performances from Seo Kang-joon as Namgung Ho and Ahn Eun-jin, who plays Lee Mi-do.
 In a video interaction, the widely popular duo chatted with t2 about the series, what holds a long-term relationship together and how an actor can emote expressly without being tangibly expressive.
 Keeping it natural 
 Advertisement In A Love Other Than Yours , as mentioned earlier, we meet Namgung Ho and Lee Mi-do at a point when they have been in a relationship for a decade, facing the expectations of family and society to take the next step — marriage. The long history between the two is shown through some flashbacks, but also implied in various ways. When asked what kinds of conversations did the co-actors have to pull that off and make us feel what was not sometimes shown on screen, Seo Kang-joon replied: “There are different kinds of ways to express love. That is true within the relationship in the series as well. We have a lot of scenes where we kiss, hold hands, hug, and express affection. But I didn’t think those moments should always feel exciting or full of butterflies. I wanted them to feel like part of the everyday life of two people who have been together for a long time.”
 Ahn Eun-jin concurred with her co-star, agreeing that the idea to keep the equation natural between Namgung Ho and Lee Mi-do is what makes the shared history between the two feel so palpable on screen. However, she did have a different take on it, too. “Since it felt completely natural, the problem arose in the relationship when excitement entered a place where there had been none. We tried hard to express comfort since the beginning where we would know each other just by looking into each other’s eyes,” the 35-year-old star of high-recall projects like The Good Bad Mother and My Dearest, told t2 .
 During our time with the two actors, we asked them, in keeping with the theme of A Love Other Than Yours , what they believed is that one factor that needs to be worked on every day to keep a romantic relationship alive? Ahn Eun-jin chimed in with: “It may sound familiar, but wouldn’t it be important to keep a sense of gratitude alive?” Seo Kang-joon elaborated further with: “You shouldn’t take it for granted that a certain person will always be beside you. But when you have been in a relationship for a long time, there may be the illusion that they will always be there, and that no matter what you do can ultimately damage the relationship.”
 Real and relatable 
 Though strong-willed, independent and ambitious, Lee Mi-do is also insecure and vulnerable, like any other human being caught in a quagmire-ish situation like hers. What is it about the character that truly resonated with her, we asked Ahn Eun-jin, who said: “Things are not going well for Lee Mi-do, and she desperately wants something. I could really understand her frustration when I first read the script. She keeps confronting sides of herself that she doesn’t want to admit are there, and she keeps thinking that the person closest to her is the reason for those feelings.”
 Advertisement “I have experienced that kind of flawed side in myself before, and so I thought I could portray those emotions well. I also thought viewers would be able to relate to Lee Mi-do through that,” she added, sporting her trademark bright and warm smile.
 The conversation circled back to the restraint in emotion and expression the show demands. How does one depict the internal turmoil of seeing a long-cherished relationship slowly slip away, especially when the characters don’t necessarily express everything they feel, was the question, for which Seo Kang-joon, 33, who was seen in last year’s Prime Video series Undercover High School, had a thoughtful, deeply articulate response: “I think that if you truly hold onto the emotions inside, they will eventually show. But I don’t know how much of that actually reaches the audience (in A Love Other Than Yours ).”
 He also cited something that Oscar winner Al Pacino, widely recognised as one of the greatest actors of all time, had said in an interview that had inspired him, particularly when it came to subtly conveying emotions.
 “Al Pacino, an actor I really respect, had said in an interview: ‘Trying to express something that I am not actually expressing isn’t good acting’. So it is important to hold onto what you are genuinely feeling inside, believe in it and trust that the camera will capture it. In  A Love Other Than Yours , I tried to approach many scenes that way, I tried not to express everything too explicitly. I don’t know how much of it came through, but I trusted that those emotions would show through my eyes, my face, and my expressions. The script also helped me understand what Namgung Ho must have been feeling.”
 Adding to it, Ahn Eun-jin was deeply appreciative of her co-star: “There is the ending scene of Episode 6. It is a scene where Namgung Ho simply listens. As he listens, you can feel his thoughts and emotions changing. It is not like he suddenly makes an obvious facial expression, yet you can clearly sense what he is thinking and how his feelings are changing. That really impressed me,” she signed off.
